entry.title: F0105 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.98): The Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy is an infinite sequence of semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations Q₁ ⊇ Q₂
entry.summary: The Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy is an infinite sequence of semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations Q₁ ⊇ Q₂ ⊇ ... ⊇ Q_k ⊇ ... ⊇ Q_c that provides outer bounds on the set of quantum correlations. Each level k is defined by the positive semidefinite constraint M⁽ᵏ⁾ ≥ 0 on the moment matrix of products of local measurement operators up to length k. The sequence converges asymptotically (k → ∞) to the set Q_c of quantum commuting correlations (where measurement operators of separate parties commute on a Hilbert space). Following the resolution of Tsirelson's problem (Ji et al., 2020, MIP* = RE), Q_c is strictly larger than the closure of the tensor-product quantum correlation set cl(Q_q), establishing that the NPA hierarchy converges to the commuting-operator quantum correlation set Q_c.

entry.title: F0106 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.97): The almost-quantum correlation set Q₁ (also denoted Q_{1+AB} or Q̃) is a semidefinite relaxation level of the NPA hierar
entry.summary: The almost-quantum correlation set Q₁ (also denoted Q_{1+AB} or Q̃) is a semidefinite relaxation level of the NPA hierarchy situated strictly between the quantum correlation set Q and the non-signaling polytope NS (Q ⊊ Q₁ ⊊ NS). Defined by positive semidefiniteness of the moment matrix constructed from operator set S = {I, A_x, B_y, A_x B_y}, Q₁ satisfies all major physical principles proposed to characterize quantum correlations—including No Advantage for Nonlocal Computation (NANLC), Information Causality (IC), Macroscopic Locality (ML), Local Orthogonality (LO), and Non-Trivial Communication Complexity (NTCC)—yet strictly contains supra-quantum correlations and violates the no-restriction hypothesis.

entry.title: F0107 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.99): The CHSH self-testing theorem establishes that maximal violation of the CHSH inequality (⟨C⟩ = 2√2) uniquely certifies,
entry.summary: The CHSH self-testing theorem establishes that maximal violation of the CHSH inequality (⟨C⟩ = 2√2) uniquely certifies, up to local isometries, the presence of a maximally entangled two-qubit state |Φ⁺⟩ = (1/√2)(|00⟩+|11⟩) and anti-commuting measurement observables. Specifically, for any state |ψ⟩ ∈ H_A ⊗ H_B and dichotomic observables A₀, A₁ on H_A and B₀, B₁ on H_B achieving ⟨ψ|A₀B₀ + A₀B₁ + A₁B₀ - A₁B₁|ψ⟩ = 2√2, there exist local isometries Φ_A: H_A → H_A' ⊗ H_A_bar and Φ_B: H_B → H_B' ⊗ H_B_bar such that (Φ_A ⊗ Φ_B)|ψ⟩ = |junk⟩ ⊗ |Φ⁺⟩, and under which A₀, A₁ and B₀, B₁ act on the target qubits as Pauli σ_z, σ_x and (σ_z + σ_x)/√2, (σ_z - σ_x)/√2.

entry.title: F0108 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.95): The Mayers-Yao self-testing protocol (Mayers & Yao, 2004) device-independently certifies a maximally entangled state |Φ⁺
entry.summary: The Mayers-Yao self-testing protocol (Mayers & Yao, 2004) device-independently certifies a maximally entangled state |Φ⁺⟩ and reference measurement choices using 3 measurement settings per party (x,y ∈ {0,1,2}). In robust self-testing, if observed correlation statistics P(ab|xy) deviate by ε in trace distance or L₁ norm from ideal target statistics, the physical state |ψ⟩ satisfies ||(Φ_A ⊗ Φ_B)|ψ⟩ - |junk⟩ ⊗ |Φ⁺⟩||₂ = O(√ε) (with O(ε) achieved under optimized robust self-testing bounds), guaranteeing quantitative state certification under experimental noise.

entry.title: F0109 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.97): Parallel self-testing protocols establish device-independent certification of N-copy tensor product states |Φ⁺⟩^{⊗N} and
entry.summary: Parallel self-testing protocols establish device-independent certification of N-copy tensor product states |Φ⁺⟩^{⊗N} and high-dimensional quantum systems (C^{2^N} ⊗ C^{2^N}) using parallelized Bell tests. Specifically, testing N maximally entangled qubit pairs simultaneously under parallel CHSH inequalities certifies that the shared state is locally isometric to |junk⟩ ⊗ (|Φ⁺⟩)^{⊗N} with a number of measurement choices per party that remains fixed at 2 (independent of N) or scales polynomial in N, enabling efficient high-dimensional quantum hardware verification.

entry.title: F0110 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.97): Self-testing rigidity characterizes the boundary ∂Q of the quantum correlation set: a correlation point P* ∈ ∂Q is rigid
entry.summary: Self-testing rigidity characterizes the boundary ∂Q of the quantum correlation set: a correlation point P* ∈ ∂Q is rigid if and only if all physical quantum realizations (H_A, H_B, |ψ⟩, {A_a^x}, {B_b^y}) yielding P* are unique up to a local isometry Φ = Φ_A ⊗ Φ_B. Exposed vector extremal points of Q that maximize linear Bell inequalities (e.g., CHSH, tilted CHSH, and CGLMP inequalities) are rigid self-tests, and every pure bipartite entangled state can be self-tested by maximal violation of an appropriate Bell inequality.

entry.title: F0099 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.99): The CHSH inequality establishes that for any local hidden-variable theory, the CHSH correlation parameter C = A₁B₁ + A₁B
entry.summary: The CHSH inequality establishes that for any local hidden-variable theory, the CHSH correlation parameter C = A₁B₁ + A₁B₂ + A₂B₁ - A₂B₂ (where A₁, A₂ are Alice's measurement outcomes with settings 1,2 and B₁, B₂ are Bob's outcomes with settings 1,2, each taking values ±1) satisfies the bound |⟨C⟩| ≤ 2. This is the classical local-realist bound derived by Clauser, Horne, Shimony, and Holt (1969).

entry.title: F0100 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.99): Tsirelson's bound states that for any bipartite quantum system in a tensor-product Hilbert space ℋ_A ⊗ ℋ_B, with dichoto
entry.summary: Tsirelson's bound states that for any bipartite quantum system in a tensor-product Hilbert space ℋ_A ⊗ ℋ_B, with dichotomic observables A₁, A₂ on ℋ_A and B₁, B₂ on ℋ_B having eigenvalues ±1, the quantum expectation value of the CHSH operator C = A₁⊗B₁ + A₁⊗B₂ + A₂⊗B₁ - A₂⊗B₂ satisfies |⟨C⟩| ≤ 2√2. This bound was derived by Boris S. Tsirelson (Cirel'son) in 1980.

entry.title: F0101 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.97): The domain assumptions for Tsirelson's bound are: (a) a bipartite Hilbert space ℋ = ℋ_A ⊗ ℋ_B of arbitrary finite or inf
entry.summary: The domain assumptions for Tsirelson's bound are: (a) a bipartite Hilbert space ℋ = ℋ_A ⊗ ℋ_B of arbitrary finite or infinite dimension; (b) Hermitian operators A₁, A₂ on ℋ_A and B₁, B₂ on ℋ_B with spectra contained in {-1, +1} (i.e., A_i² = I, B_j² = I); (c) the CHSH operator is C = A₁⊗B₁ + A₁⊗B₂ + A₂⊗B₁ - A₂⊗B₂. The bound |⟨C⟩| ≤ 2√2 is saturated if and only if the state is a maximally entangled two-qubit state (locally equivalent to the singlet) and the observables satisfy the anti-commutation relations {A₁,A₂} = 0, {B₁,B₂} = 0 with appropriate relative angles (e.g., 45° between A₁,A₂ and 22.5° between Bob's settings and Alice's).

entry.title: F0102 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.99): The non-signaling principle alone permits correlations up to the algebraic maximum of the CHSH expression: |⟨C⟩| ≤ 4. Po
entry.summary: The non-signaling principle alone permits correlations up to the algebraic maximum of the CHSH expression: |⟨C⟩| ≤ 4. Popescu-Rohrlich (PR) boxes are hypothetical non-signaling correlations that achieve |⟨C⟩| = 4, defined by P(a,b|x,y) = 1/2 if a⊕b = x·y (mod 2) and 0 otherwise, for inputs x,y ∈ {0,1} and outputs a,b ∈ {0,1}. This demonstrates that quantum mechanics (bound 2√2 ≈ 2.828) is strictly more constrained than the non-signaling polytope.

entry.title: F0103 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.99): The Kochen-Specker theorem (Kochen & Specker, 1967; Bell, 1966) proves that for any Hilbert space of dimension d ≥ 3, th
entry.summary: The Kochen-Specker theorem (Kochen & Specker, 1967; Bell, 1966) proves that for any Hilbert space of dimension d ≥ 3, there is no non-contextual hidden-variable theory that assigns definite values (0 or 1) to all projection operators (or equivalently, to all yes-no observables) such that: (i) the value assigned to the identity operator is 1; (ii) for any set of mutually orthogonal projections summing to identity, exactly one is assigned value 1. This establishes quantum contextuality: measurement outcomes cannot be pre-determined independently of the measurement context (which compatible observables are measured jointly).

entry.title: F0104 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.98): The CHSH inequality and Tsirelson's bound have been formally verified in the Isabelle/HOL proof assistant by Echenim and
entry.summary: The CHSH inequality and Tsirelson's bound have been formally verified in the Isabelle/HOL proof assistant by Echenim and Mhalla (2023, arXiv:2306.12535). The formalization includes density matrices, projective measurements, the CHSH inequality proof (|⟨C⟩| ≤ 2 for local hidden variables), and Tsirelson's bound (|⟨C⟩| ≤ 2√2 for quantum mechanics), providing machine-checkable verification of these foundational results.

Key findings: (1) CHSH inequality classical bound |⟨C⟩| ≤ 2 (Clauser et al. 1969); (2) Tsirelson's bound |⟨C⟩| ≤ 2√2 for quantum correlations (Tsirelson 1980, Lett. Math. All claims are verifiable with explicit mathematical statements and refutation conditions.

entry.title: F0089 (superseded, verifiable, confidence 0.97): Berta et al. (2010) Entropic Uncertainty Relation with Quantum Memory (EUR-QM): For any bipartite state rho_{AB} shared
entry.summary: Berta et al. (2010) Entropic Uncertainty Relation with Quantum Memory (EUR-QM): For any bipartite state rho_{AB} shared between Alice (system A) and an observer holding quantum memory (system B), when Alice measures observable X (with eigenbasis {|x_i>}) or Z (with eigenbasis {|z_j>}), the conditional Shannon/von Neumann entropies satisfy S(X|B) + S(Z|B) ≥ log₂(1/c) + S(A|B), where S(X|B) = H(X|_B) is the conditional Shannon entropy of measurement outcomes given B, c = max_{i,j} |<x_i|z_j>| is the maximum overlap between the two measurement bases, and S(A|B) is the conditional von Neumann entropy of state A given quantum memory B.

entry.title: F0090 (superseded, verifiable, confidence 0.85): Purification and Tripartite Formulation: The Berta et al. entropic uncertainty relation is derived by considering a puri
entry.summary: Purification and Tripartite Formulation: The Berta et al. entropic uncertainty relation is derived by considering a purification of the bipartite state rho_{AB} to a pure tripartite state |psi>_{ABE} on systems A, B, and E (where E is the reference/environment system). By relating the conditional entropy S(X|B) to the entropy S(X|E) on the purifying system, the tradeoff inequality S(X|B) + S(Z|B) ≥ log₂(1/c) + S(A|B) is shown to be equivalent to S(X|B) + S(Z|E) ≥ log₂(1/c), reflecting the trade-off between the observer's ability to predict measurement outcomes via quantum memory B versus the eavesdropper/reference E's accessible information.

entry.title: F0091 (superseded, verifiable, confidence 0.85): Domain Boundaries and Limit Behavior of EUR-QM: (1) The Hilbert space dimensions of system A (dim A = d_A) and quantum m
entry.summary: Domain Boundaries and Limit Behavior of EUR-QM: (1) The Hilbert space dimensions of system A (dim A = d_A) and quantum memory B (dim B = d_B) can be finite or infinite, provided all density operators have well-defined, finite von Neumann entropies. (2) When system A is maximally entangled with quantum memory B (e.g., in a maximally entangled state), S(A|B) = -log₂(d_A), allowing the lower bound log₂(1/c) + S(A|B) to become zero or negative, meaning both incompatible measurements can be predicted with arbitrary certainty (beating classical uncertainty limits). (3) When B is trivial (classical or empty), S(A|B) = S(A) ≥ 0, recovering the standard Maassen-Uffink bound.

entry.title: F0092 (superseded, verifiable, confidence 0.85): Subsequent Tightenings with Quantum Side Information: The Berta et al. lower bound S(X|B) + S(Z|B) ≥ log₂(1/c) + S(A|B)
entry.summary: Subsequent Tightenings with Quantum Side Information: The Berta et al. lower bound S(X|B) + S(Z|B) ≥ log₂(1/c) + S(A|B) can be strictly tightened by incorporating state-dependent quantum correlation measures such as quantum discord and classical correlations (Pati et al., 2012) or measurement-reversibility / disturbance terms (Coles, Berta, and Wilde, 2012; Berta, Wehner, and Wilde, 2015). For instance, Coles-Piani (2014) and related refinements add non-negative terms capturing the residual incompatibility and information gain of the specific measurement process beyond the basis overlap c.

entry.title: F0093 (superseded, verifiable, confidence 0.85): Applications to Quantum Cryptography and Quantum Steering: The entropic uncertainty relation with quantum memory serves
entry.summary: Applications to Quantum Cryptography and Quantum Steering: The entropic uncertainty relation with quantum memory serves as a foundational tool for proving the security of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols (such as BB84 and six-state protocols) against general collective and coherent attacks, without requiring the BB84 source to be characterized or trusted by the receiver (device-independent and source-device-independent frameworks). Furthermore, violations of entropic uncertainty bounds with quantum side information provide quantitative witnesses for entanglement and quantum steering (demonstrating that an observer's reduction in uncertainty can only be achieved if system A is entangled with quantum memory B).

entry.title: F0094 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.98): Corrected Berta et al. (2010) Entropic Uncertainty Relation with Quantum Memory (EUR-QM): For any bipartite quantum stat
entry.summary: Corrected Berta et al. (2010) Entropic Uncertainty Relation with Quantum Memory (EUR-QM): For any bipartite quantum state ρ_AB on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces H_A ⊗ H_B, when Alice measures observable X (eigenbasis {|x_i>}) or Z (eigenbasis {|z_j>}) on system A, the conditional entropies satisfy S(X|B) + S(Z|B) ≥ log₂(1/c) + S(A|B), where c = max_{i,j} |<x_i|z_j>|² is the squared overlap of the measurement bases. Equivalently, the lower bound is -2 log₂(max_{i,j} |<x_i|z_j>|) + S(A|B). Here S(X|B) is the conditional Shannon/von Neumann entropy of measurement outcome X given quantum memory B, and S(A|B) = S(ρ_AB) - S(ρ_B) is the conditional von Neumann entropy.

entry.title: F0095 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.96): Purification and Tripartite Lemma Derivation of EUR-QM: The derivation of the Berta et al. entropic uncertainty relation
entry.summary: Purification and Tripartite Lemma Derivation of EUR-QM: The derivation of the Berta et al. entropic uncertainty relation considers a purification |ψ>_ABE of the bipartite state ρ_AB by adding a purifying reference system E. Using the data-processing inequality for quantum relative entropy and the duality property of conditional von Neumann entropy S(X|B) = -S(X|E) for pure tripartite states, one derives the tripartite inequality S(X|B) + S(Z|E) ≥ log₂(1/c) as an intermediate lemma, which directly yields S(X|B) + S(Z|B) ≥ log₂(1/c) + S(A|B). The tripartite form is a key proof lemma rather than an equivalent restatement of the bipartite relation.

entry.title: F0096 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.96): Domain Boundaries and Limit Behavior of EUR-QM: (1) The original Berta et al. (2010) paper was established for finite-di
entry.summary: Domain Boundaries and Limit Behavior of EUR-QM: (1) The original Berta et al. (2010) paper was established for finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces (dim H_A < ∞); extensions to infinite-dimensional continuous-variable (CV) systems were proven later by Furrer, Franz, Berta et al. (2012, Phys. Rev. Lett. 109, 100502) and Tomamichel, Berta, Renes (2013). (2) When system A is maximally entangled with quantum memory B (dim H_A = d_A), S(A|B) = -log₂(d_A); for mutually unbiased bases (c = 1/d_A), the bound log₂(1/c) + S(A|B) becomes zero, allowing complete outcome predictability S(X|B) = S(Z|B) = 0. (3) When B is trivial (classical or 1-dimensional), S(A|B) = S(A) ≥ 0, recovering the standard Maassen-Uffink bound.

entry.title: F0097 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.96): State-Dependent Tightenings of EUR-QM: The Berta et al. lower bound log₂(1/c) + S(A|B) can be strictly tightened by addi
entry.summary: State-Dependent Tightenings of EUR-QM: The Berta et al. lower bound log₂(1/c) + S(A|B) can be strictly tightened by adding state-dependent correlation terms: (a) Pati, Devi, Maccone et al. (2012, Phys. Rev. A 86, 042105 / arXiv:1111.0984) incorporated quantum discord and classical correlations; (b) Coles and Piani (2014, Phys. Rev. Lett. 113, 030402 / arXiv:1402.7197) added terms depending on secondary overlaps and state entropy; (c) Coles, Berta, Tomamichel, Wilde, and Wehner (2015/2017, Rev. Mod. Phys. 89, 015002 / arXiv:1511.04857) established unified entropic uncertainty relations incorporating non-negative measurement reversibility and disturbance terms.

entry.title: F0098 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.95): EUR-QM Applications in QKD Security Frameworks and Quantum Steering: Entropic uncertainty relations with quantum memory
entry.summary: EUR-QM Applications in QKD Security Frameworks and Quantum Steering: Entropic uncertainty relations with quantum memory provide foundational lower bounds on key extraction rates in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD): (a) In standard BB84 and six-state QKD protocols, EUR-QM bounds secret key generation rates under coherent attacks assuming trusted, characterized source and measurement devices; (b) Device-Independent QKD (DI-QKD) and Source-Device-Independent QKD (SDI-QKD) represent distinct cryptographic frameworks with relaxed device-trust assumptions that also utilize entropic uncertainty bounds as core security steps; (c) Violations of classical entropic uncertainty inequalities in the presence of quantum side information act as quantitative witnesses for quantum entanglement and quantum steering.

entry.title: F0081 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.98): Holevo's bound (Holevo's theorem): For an ensemble of quantum states {p_x, ρ_x} with probabilities p_x ≥ 0, ∑_x p_x = 1,
entry.summary: Holevo's bound (Holevo's theorem): For an ensemble of quantum states {p_x, ρ_x} with probabilities p_x ≥ 0, ∑_x p_x = 1, and density operators ρ_x on a Hilbert space H, the accessible information I_acc — the maximum classical mutual information I(X:Y) obtainable by any measurement {E_y} (POVM) on the ensemble — satisfies I_acc ≤ χ, where χ = S(∑_x p_x ρ_x) - ∑_x p_x S(ρ_x) is the Holevo quantity, and S(ρ) = -Tr(ρ log ρ) is the von Neumann entropy (log base 2 for bits, or natural log for nats).

entry.title: F0082 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.95): Domain boundaries and validity conditions for Holevo's bound: (1) The Hilbert space H may be finite-dimensional or separ
entry.summary: Domain boundaries and validity conditions for Holevo's bound: (1) The Hilbert space H may be finite-dimensional or separable infinite-dimensional; (2) The ensemble {p_x, ρ_x} may be discrete (finite or countably infinite) with ∑_x p_x = 1; (3) Each ρ_x is a density operator (positive semidefinite, trace 1); (4) The von Neumann entropies S(ρ_x) and S(∑_x p_x ρ_x) must be finite (or the bound is interpreted with extended real values, where S(ρ) = +∞ for states with infinite entropy); (5) The bound holds for arbitrary POVMs {E_y} with ∑_y E_y = I, E_y ≥ 0; (6) For continuous-variable systems with infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, the bound holds when all entropies are finite, but may require regularization (e.g., energy constraints) to avoid trivial infinite bounds.

entry.title: F0083 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.97): Maassen-Uffink entropic uncertainty relation (general form): For a quantum system in a pure state |ψ⟩ ∈ H (dim H = d < ∞
entry.summary: Maassen-Uffink entropic uncertainty relation (general form): For a quantum system in a pure state |ψ⟩ ∈ H (dim H = d < ∞), and two observables A = ∑_i a_i |a_i⟩⟨a_i|, B = ∑_j b_j |b_j⟩⟨b_j| with non-degenerate discrete spectra and eigenbases {|a_i⟩}, {|b_j⟩}, the Shannon entropies of the measurement outcome distributions satisfy H(A) + H(B) ≥ -2 log₂ c, where H(A) = -∑_i |⟨a_i|ψ⟩|² log₂ |⟨a_i|ψ⟩|², H(B) = -∑_j |⟨b_j|ψ⟩|² log₂ |⟨b_j|ψ⟩|², and c = max_{i,j} |⟨a_i|b_j⟩| is the maximum overlap between the two eigenbases. (Log base 2 gives bits; natural log gives nats with factor 1/ln 2 adjustment.)

entry.title: F0084 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.98): Maassen-Uffink relation for mutually unbiased bases (MUBs): If {|a_i⟩} and {|b_j⟩} are mutually unbiased bases in dimens
entry.summary: Maassen-Uffink relation for mutually unbiased bases (MUBs): If {|a_i⟩} and {|b_j⟩} are mutually unbiased bases in dimension d (i.e., |⟨a_i|b_j⟩|² = 1/d for all i, j), then c = max_{i,j} |⟨a_i|b_j⟩| = 1/√d, and the entropic uncertainty relation becomes H(A) + H(B) ≥ log₂ d. This bound is tight: there exist states (e.g., any eigenstate of A or B) that saturate it.

entry.title: F0085 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.93): Domain boundaries and validity conditions for the Maassen-Uffink relation: (1) The Hilbert space H is finite-dimensional
entry.summary: Domain boundaries and validity conditions for the Maassen-Uffink relation: (1) The Hilbert space H is finite-dimensional (d < ∞); (2) The state |ψ⟩ is pure (can be extended to mixed states via the concave roof / purification, giving H(A)+H(B) ≥ -2 log₂ c for any ρ, where H(A) = -∑_i ⟨a_i|ρ|a_i⟩ log ⟨a_i|ρ|a_i⟩); (3) Observables A and B have non-degenerate discrete spectra (or more generally, are described by projective measurements with projectors {|a_i⟩⟨a_i|}, {|b_j⟩⟨b_j|}); (4) The overlap c = max_{i,j} |⟨a_i|b_j⟩| is well-defined and < 1 (if c = 1, the bound is trivial: H(A)+H(B) ≥ 0); (5) For infinite-dimensional systems (e.g., position and momentum), the relation holds with c = 1/√(2πħ) for conjugate variables, but requires careful treatment of continuous Shannon entropy (differential entropy) and domain restrictions (e.g., states in the Schwartz space).

entry.title: F0086 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.90): The Maassen-Uffink bound H(A) + H(B) ≥ -2 log₂ c is not universally optimal: for some pairs of observables, there exist
entry.summary: The Maassen-Uffink bound H(A) + H(B) ≥ -2 log₂ c is not universally optimal: for some pairs of observables, there exist tighter state-dependent lower bounds (e.g., the 'optimal' uncertainty relations of Friedland, Gheorghiu, and Gour 2013; or the majorization-based bounds of Puchała, Rudnicki, and Życzkowski 2013). However, the Maassen-Uffink bound is optimal among all bounds that depend only on the maximum overlap c and not on the full structure of the unitary relating the two bases.

entry.title: F0087 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.95): Holevo capacity of a quantum channel: For a quantum channel Φ: L(H_A) → L(H_B) (completely positive trace-preserving map
entry.summary: Holevo capacity of a quantum channel: For a quantum channel Φ: L(H_A) → L(H_B) (completely positive trace-preserving map), the classical capacity with product state encodings (Holevo capacity) is C(Φ) = max_{p_x, ρ_x} χ({p_x, Φ(ρ_x)}), where the maximum is over all ensembles {p_x, ρ_x} of input states. This is the maximum rate at which classical information can be transmitted reliably through the channel using product-state coding (no entanglement between channel uses). The full classical capacity (with entangled encodings) is the regularization C_∞(Φ) = lim_{n→∞} C(Φ^{⊗n})/n.

entry.title: F0088 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.94): Tightness of Holevo's bound: The bound I_acc ≤ χ is asymptotically attainable: for any ensemble {p_x, ρ_x}, there exists
entry.summary: Tightness of Holevo's bound: The bound I_acc ≤ χ is asymptotically attainable: for any ensemble {p_x, ρ_x}, there exists a sequence of collective measurements on n copies of the states such that the accessible information per copy approaches χ as n → ∞ (Holevo-Schumacher-Westmoreland theorem). For single-copy measurements (without collective measurements on multiple copies), the bound is generally not tight — the maximum single-copy accessible information can be strictly less than χ (e.g., for certain symmetric ensembles like the 'trine' states or 'quantum pyramids').

entry.title: F0077 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.98): The Mandelstam-Tamm (MT) quantum speed limit bounds the minimum evolution time \tau between an initial pure state |\psi(
entry.summary: The Mandelstam-Tamm (MT) quantum speed limit bounds the minimum evolution time \tau between an initial pure state |\psi(0)\rangle and an orthogonal (or distinguishably evolved) final state under a time-independent Hamiltonian H as \tau \geq \frac{\pi \hbar}{2 \Delta E}, where \Delta E = \sqrt{\langle H^2 \rangle - \langle H \rangle^2} is the energy standard deviation (dispersion) in the state. For mixed states, \Delta E is replaced by the Bures-angle rate or variance \Delta H.

entry.title: F0078 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.96): Domain boundaries and validity conditions for the Mandelstam-Tamm speed limit require: (1) A Hilbert space \mathcal{H} o
entry.summary: Domain boundaries and validity conditions for the Mandelstam-Tamm speed limit require: (1) A Hilbert space \mathcal{H} of arbitrary dimension (finite or infinite); (2) A time-independent Hermitian Hamiltonian operator H bounded from below with a well-defined finite energy dispersion \Delta E < \infty; (3) Pure or mixed states \rho(t) undergoing unitary evolution via the von Neumann / Schrödinger equation \partial_t \rho = -\frac{i}{\hbar}[H, \rho]. For systems with infinite energy dispersion (\Delta E \to \infty), the Mandelstam-Tamm bound becomes trivial (\tau \geq 0), necessitating complementary bounds such as Margolus-Levitin.

entry.title: F0079 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.98): The Margolus-Levitin (ML) theorem bounds the minimum evolution time \tau for a quantum system to evolve from an initial
entry.summary: The Margolus-Levitin (ML) theorem bounds the minimum evolution time \tau for a quantum system to evolve from an initial state \psi(0) to an orthogonal state \psi(\tau) \langle \psi(0)|\psi(\tau) \rangle = 0 under a time-independent Hamiltonian H with ground state energy set to zero (E_0 = 0), given by \tau \geq \frac{\pi \hbar}{2 \langle H \rangle}, where \langle H \rangle = \langle \psi(0)| H |\psi(0) \rangle$ is the mean excitation energy above the ground state.

entry.title: F0080 (supported, verifiable, confidence 0.97): Domain boundaries and complementary utility of the Margolus-Levitin theorem require: (1) A quantum system governed by a
entry.summary: Domain boundaries and complementary utility of the Margolus-Levitin theorem require: (1) A quantum system governed by a time-independent Hamiltonian H bounded from below (with ground state energy convention E_0 = 0); (2) Finite mean excitation energy \langle H \rangle < \infty; (3) The bound is tightest when the energy dispersion \Delta E is large compared to \langle H \rangle (e.g., for multi-level superposition states with high-frequency components), whereas the Mandelstam-Tamm bound is tightest when \Delta E is small compared to \langle H \rangle (e.g., for narrow two-level systems). Combining both yields the unified quantum speed limit \tau \geq \max \left( \frac{\pi \hbar}{2 \Delta E}, \frac{\pi \hbar}{2 \langle H \rangle} \right).
